quirks.condition: A sender's 3rd, 6th, 9th and every further 3rd accepted LODGE of the session.
quirks.effect: Rounds dispatch by a hidden per-parcel priority that starts at the declared heft; such a parcel's priority is raised by 15 points at shelving, so it can leave ahead of heavier parcels. The spec dispatches by declared heft alone.

quirks.condition: A LODGE accepted after its sender has already had 2 or more accepted BOUNCE reports (on any parcels).
quirks.effect: The parcel's dispatch priority is lowered by 10 points at shelving, so it can leave behind lighter parcels. The spec dispatches by declared heft alone.

quirks.condition: A bay parcel shelved onto a lane that has already run w accepted ROUND commands (VOID rounds included), with w greater than 0.
quirks.effect: The parcel's dispatch priority is lowered by 5 points per accepted round on the lane (5 times w), so fresh parcels on worn lanes can leave behind older, lighter parcels. The spec dispatches by declared heft alone.

quirks.condition: A ROUND on a lane that has already run 3 or more accepted ROUND commands (VOID rounds included).
quirks.effect: At most 3 parcels are dispatched instead of the spec's 4; the RAN count reflects the shorter cap.

quirks.condition: Any dispatch-priority value produced by an adjustment (raise, lowering, wear lowering, or return lowering) on either the live shelving path or the seasonal replay, when the adjusted value differs from the declared heft.
quirks.effect: A value below 1 is clamped to 1, and a value that is an exact multiple of 25 is raised by 1 point, so a parcel that would otherwise tie on a multiple of 25 leaves ahead of a rival with the same priority; a parcel whose priority still equals its heft is not adjusted. The spec has no such step.

quirks.condition: A bounced parcel is moved from the return ledge back onto its lane's shelf by SHELVE.
quirks.effect: Its dispatch priority is lowered by 40 points on every re-shelving, accumulating across repeated bounces, so it can leave behind lighter parcels. The spec re-shelves it as if newly arrived at its declared heft.

quirks.condition: SHELVE with bay parcels destined for more than one lane.
quirks.effect: PUT lines and shelf placement are grouped by lane in lane-open order, lodge order preserved within each lane, instead of the spec's single pass in lodge order.

quirks.condition: SHELVE while parcels sit on the return ledge.
quirks.effect: Ledge parcels are placed first, ahead of the day's bay arrivals, and keep their original arrival stamps for tie-breaking, instead of the spec's placement behind the arrivals as if newly arrived.

quirks.condition: HELD for a sender with parcels on more than one lane's shelf.
quirks.effect: The FOR listing is grouped by lane in lane-open order, shelf order within each lane, instead of the spec's arrival order across lanes.

The posted listings are rebuilt by replaying the event ledger and then overwrite the live shelves, priorities, stamps, and lane wear: parcels still in the bay or on the return ledge are pulled onto their shelves, a bounced parcel is placed at the point in the walk where its bounce was recorded, arrival stamps are reassigned in walk order, and the open return window is closed so later BOUNCE reports are rejected STATE. The spec says the recount changes nothing.

quirks.condition: SQUARE after one or more VOID rounds on a lane.
quirks.effect: VOID rounds were never written to the ledger, so the replayed wear count (accepted rounds per lane) omits them and the lower count is written back over the live count, changing later wear lowering and round caps; the spec counts every accepted ROUND.

quirks.condition: SQUARE after a parcel has bounced more than once, or after a sender's bounce tally reached 2 through repeated bounces of one parcel.
quirks.effect: The ledger keeps only each parcel's most recent bounce position, so the replay applies a single 40-point return lowering per parcel, and earlier bounces vanish from the sender's tally used for the 10-point lowering; the rebuilt shelf order therefore differs from the live order that accumulated per bounce.

quirks.condition: SQUARE after a WAIVE of a parcel that was in the bay or on a shelf.
quirks.effect: Withdrawals were never written to the ledger, so the replay puts the withdrawn parcel back on its lane's shelf, where it is listed, dispatched, and can be waived again; the spec says a withdrawn parcel is gone for good.

unmapped_families.reason: Mixed held-out corpus of long random sessions exercising every rule above together with strict validation; no single quirk maps.

Gold and legacy/run both print, after OK 4: OUT a3, OUT b1, OUT a1, OUT a2, RAN north 4, trailer X 2 1 4 1 0 0 0.

Then ann lodges m1 (heft 600), bob lodges m2 (heft 500), ann lodges m3 (heft 400), bob lodges m4 (heft 300), all onto east. Then SHELVE, then ROUND east. What number appears at the end of the final RAN line?
reader_questions.verification: Stream: REG ann / REG bob / LANE east / LODGE ann k1 east 100 / SHELVE / ROUND east / ROUND east / ROUND east / LODGE ann m1 east 600 / LODGE bob m2 east 500 / LODGE ann m3 east 400 / LODGE bob m4 east 300 / SHELVE / ROUND east / LIST east. Gold and legacy/run both print: OUT k1, RAN east 1, VOID east, VOID east, ... OK 4, OUT m1, OUT m2, OUT m3, RAN east 3, SHELF east m4, trailer X 2 1 5 4 0 0 0.
